context:
Goal: an undo after a restore never removes a check-in the restore brought back.
Problem (rule): today a Recent row stays live while the card's last-saved time is at or after the row's time. A restore stamps every card with the restore time, so every old row passes. Probe: a count is 1, a row moves it to 2, you restore to 1, and undoing the row sets it to 0.
Based on (read): the native app restores today (native-parity-table, lane N9) and writes no log entry and no new field until debt recent-log-unbuilt ships. So b alone misses a phone restore: the web rows stay live, and an undo removes what the restore brought back.
Based on (read): b needs more than one field: six write sites, new pins in test groups 9, 37 and 39, a merge rule in mergeLedger, and Worker tests for it.
Departs from: recent-checks-can-be-undone, "last-saved time at or after the row's time" — becomes "last-saved time equals the newest log entry on this card" (a).
Meanwhile: the lane builds a.
holds: When a mailaudit Recent row can still be undone after a restore.

lastAnswer.note: isnt storing the restore time better

options.gain: Covers every restore, the phone's included, with no new field.
options.how: A row is live only while the card's last change came from a log entry. Any restore, by any device or build, makes old rows read NOTHING TO UNDO.
options.label: Live only while the card's last save is the row's
options.lose: After a phone check on a card, that card's older web rows read NOTHING TO UNDO, until the phone app logs its changes.

options.how: The undo log stores when the last restore happened, and rows older than it go inert.
options.label: Store the restore time
options.lose: Misses a restore from the phone or an older web build, which is the bug it is meant to fix. Needs six write sites, new test pins, a merge rule and Worker tests. Safe only together with a, at double the cost.

reply: Built in mailaudit #208 (lane mailaudit-recent-log, 17:10 CST). It stores no restore time: the phone app restores without a Recent log, so a stored time would miss those restores. The rule instead: after a restore, an old row can be undone only while the card still holds the count that row left. Test R4.5 shows a restore to 1 makes the 1-to-2 row read NOTHING TO UNDO. It failed on the first build and passes on #208. This closes when #208 merges.
title: mailaudit: after a restore, an undo can remove a check-in the restore brought back. Which test decides a Recent row is still live?
why: An undo that removes restored data loses a check-in you meant to keep.
